drug_class: COX-2 inhibitor (a type of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, or NSAID)
purpose: Celecoxib is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by conditions like arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It can also help with acute pain, such as pain after surgery or from menstrual cramps. Basically, it helps you feel more comfortable and move more easily when inflammation is causing you problems.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called COX-2 when there is injury or inflammation, and this chemical causes pain and swelling. Celecoxib works by specifically blocking COX-2, which reduces the chemicals that cause that pain and swelling. Unlike older pain relievers like ibuprofen, it tries to leave the stomach-protecting chemicals alone, which may be gentler on your stomach.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, heartburn, or belly pain are the most common issues. Some people get headaches, dizziness, or swelling in their hands and feet. You might also notice mild skin reactions or a runny nose.
warnings: This medicine can raise your risk of heart attack or stroke, especially if taken at high doses or for a long time, so let your doctor know if you have heart disease. It can also cause serious stomach bleeding or ulcers. Avoid it if you are allergic to sulfonamide drugs or aspirin. Do not take it during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months. Always tell your doctor about all medicines you take, since celecoxib can interact with blood thinners, other NSAIDs, and certain blood pressure medicines.
typical_dosing: For arthritis, a common dose is 100 mg to 200 mg taken once or twice a day. For short-term pain relief, doctors often prescribe 400 mg on the first day, then 200 mg twice daily as needed. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and take it with food or milk if it bothers your stomach.
